expected.name: Charles Doy
expected.description: Charles Doy was the nineteen-year-old son of Underground Railroad conductor John Doy. He accompanied his father and thirteen Black passengers on a January 1859 journey from Lawrence, Kansas Territory, toward Nebraska. Armed Missourians seized the party on January 25 and carried John and Charles across the state line, where both were committed to jail on allegations of abducting enslaved people. Charles remained imprisoned at Platte City until the first trial at St. Joseph on March 20, when prosecutors abandoned the case against him and released him. He later joined the Kansas party that returned to St. Joseph and rescued his father from jail.
